title: Bacillus velezensis S141: A Soybean Growth-Promoting Rhizosphere Bacterium
content: Soybeans depend on interactions with rhizospheric microorganisms to support and enhance their growth. Bacillus velezensis S141 is a soybean growth-promoting bacterium, originally isolated from rhizosphere soil in Thailand. This review describes a general overview of growth promotion in plants, particularly soybeans, by rhizobial interactions, followed by an introduction to the current state of our research, specifically focused on S141. S141 stimulates soybean development by producing hormones, enhancing nodulation with Bradyrhizobium species, and improving nitrogen fixation. It may also hydrolyse isoflavone glucosides and improve root growth under drought conditions. Consequently, this bacterial strain has the potential to function as a valuable bio-inoculant in sustainable agriculture.
